Thanks Alice — good summary. High level: both of your preferred approaches are supported but have tradeoffs. I'll outline three practical patterns and then a recommended action plan.

Patterns (tradeoffs):

1) Internal CA + offline CSR (recommended for regulated setups)
   - You generate a CSR per FQDN and deliver it to Redwood (we provide a CSR template).
   - You sign with your internal CA and upload the certificate and chain to the Private runtime's keystore.
   - Pros: full control, fits offline/air‑gapped environments, aligns with internal audit.
   - Cons: cert rotation handled by you; Redwood can automate reloads but schedule needs coordination.

2) Split‑horizon DNS + internal challenge (CNAME/A delegation)
   - Create internal A/CNAME entries in your private DNS that resolve to your LB or to an internal Redwood ingress endpoint (if you use Redwood-managed private DNS inside the VPC).
   - Redwood validates via http-01 or tls-alpn-01 from inside the VPC (no public exposure).
   - Pros: automated issuance/renewal, minimal manual rotation.
   - Cons: requires internal DNS changes and a routable path for the challenge.

3) Edge termination at customer's LB + mTLS to Redwood (client certs)
   - You terminate TLS at your LB with your cert, and configure mTLS from your LB -> Redwood service to authenticate requests.
   - Pros: you control TLS for client connections; Redwood only needs client certs for trust.
   - Cons: more complex proxy config and operational overhead for mutual cert rotation.

Recommended action (stepwise):
- Short term (pilot): Use offline CSR for the initial rollout so you avoid DNS churn. We'll provide the CSR template and a simple upload endpoint.
- Mid term: Set up split‑horizon DNS + internal http-01 once the VPC routing is stable so we can automate renewals.
- Long term: Evaluate mTLS if you want the LB to perform TLS termination for end users and maintain zero trust between LB and Redwood.

Operational details and deliverables from Redwood:
- CSR template + cert upload guide (we will provide).
- A rotation calendar template (we recommend 90‑day certs with automation hooks; we can support 30/60/90 day cadences).
- A short runbook for reloading certs into the Private runtime without service interruption (preparing a hot swap on the keystore).

Action items for Acme:
1) Decide pilot route (offline CSR vs split‑horizon).
2) If offline CSR: generate one CSR for the primary host and share (we'll validate in staging).
3) If split‑horizon: share internal DNS zone admin contact and a temporary test A record.

I've attached a quick checklist we use for handoffs. If this looks good, Marissa and Karthik can help run the swap.

Best,

+1 to Jonas's phased approach. A couple of implementation notes from infra/SRE perspective:

- If you pick offline CSR: please include the full chain and intermediate certs when you upload. Our keystore requires the server cert followed by intermediates.
- For rotation: we can automate a cert fetch job if you drop the signed cert at an internal S3/GCS bucket (pre-signed URL) and give us read-only access. This lets us perform zero-downtime keystore swaps.
- For split‑horizon: ensure TTLs are low for the pilot records (60–120s) so we can test quick rollback.

I'll send a short doc that maps our keystore formats and the exact import CLI. Also happy to run a 30 minute runbook session with your infra team.
